NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>SOURCE shows one two-storey white volume from the front-left: thin roof coping, two upper glazed door bays, one wide ground-floor glazed opening, two stacked narrow left-wall windows, a projecting glass balcony, a full-height timber strip at front-right, grey plinth and surrounding paved terrace. CURRENT captures these principal facade elements but misplaces the balcony’s right termination, alters the side-window proportions and omits the terrace. Rear/right elevations and roof surface are unobserved in SOURCE; their fidelity cannot be established. Screenshots show apparent balcony attachment but cannot verify concealed joints.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: CURRENT’s balcony extends beyond the right building edge in the source-matched view. SOURCE terminates it slightly inside that edge, in front of the timber strip.
action: Shorten the balcony slab and front railing at the right end; relocate the return together so it meets the facade without floating or crossing the corner.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="left">problem: CURRENT’s stacked side windows read as thinner, taller slits with conspicuous central mullions. SOURCE shows broader narrow windows with a single dominant glazed field.
action: Locally widen and shorten both openings and simplify their internal framing, preserving their stacked alignment and existing position along the wall.</issue>
<issue priority="3" view="front">problem: SOURCE has a paved terrace projecting beyond the front and visible left wall. CURRENT ends at the narrow grey building base, omitting this visible ground-level geometry.
action: Add a shallow terrace slab extending along those observed edges, keeping it distinct from the grey wall plinth.</issue>
<keep>Two separate upper front glazed bays.
One wide ground-floor front opening with a central division.
Full-height vertical timber treatment at the front-right edge.
Thin coping along the visible roof edges.</keep>
